messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH: gpu-provision-queue growth in prod-us-west-2 — autoscaler failing to add GPU nodes. Pager escalated to #incidents and oncall. Thread root ts=1719000000
harper (oncall): seeing big backlog visible in metrics, queue up 12k, token throttles spiking. Can folks jump in?
kim (support): multiple customer-facing errors: 429 /backend/serve generate throttled or queued for >30s. CS is getting tickets from 3 accounts.
sanjeev: checked cluster-autoscaler logs -> repeatedly attempts to create nodegroup but API calls failing with 403 when attaching instance profile. Error snippet below:
```
E0415 15:10:05.123456 1 aws_client.go:342] AttachRolePolicy failed: AccessDenied: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/redwood-provisioner is not authorized to perform: iam:AttachRolePolicy on resource: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-gpu-node
status code: 403, request id: 7b3b...
```
marta: that 403 lines up with last night's IAM automation rollout — could be the new least-priv policy removed attach privileges. Esteban, any changes from infra?
esteban (infra): I pushed an IAM policy drift correction to infra repo earlier but it was targeted at dedicated accounts only. Not prod. No automated change in prod. However I see new launch template version id mismatch: autoscaler requests lt v5 but ASG default lt is v4. Cloud returned "InvalidLaunchTemplateVersion: version '5' does not exist" in some attempts. Combined with 403 from IAM when trying to tag/attach.
harper (oncall): so two failure modes: launchtemplate version mismatch + IAM attach 403. Which is blocking nodes from provisioning. Need a mitigation plan: reduce queue, failover, or manually provision.
sanjeev: immediate mitigations: 1) open temporary soft-limit bump to allow CPU-only fallback for non-latency customers; 2) manually create a GPU nodegroup with a working launch template v4 and correct instance profile; 3) revert IAM rollout if it indeed removed attach permissions.
leo: I'm spinning up a manual ASG using launch-template v4 and instance-profile redwood-gpu-node-prod. Will try to attach via console to rule out automated-role attach issues.
kim (support): can we communicate to affected customers? CS will post a status note indicating degraded throughput and ETA 2h while mitigation proceeds.
esteban (infra): confirming autoscaler attempted to create nodegroup with template version v5 because of a bad mapping in terraform state for prod. I'll run a quick patch to point mapping back to v4, but terraform apply needs approval from infra-owners.
marta: if terraform apply will take 20-30m, do manual creation now. Harper, do you have cloud console access?
harper (oncall): I do. Leo, can you paste the exact ASG create command? I'll run it.
leo: console steps I used:
```
aws autoscaling create-auto-scaling-group \
  --auto-scaling-group-name redwood-gpu-temp-1719 \
  --launch-template LaunchTemplateId=lt-0abcd1234,Version=4 \
  --min-size 1 --max-size 4 --desired-capacity 2 \
  --vpc-zone-identifier subnet-aaa,subnet-bbb
```
leo: after creation, I manually attached instance profile and set taints to "node.kubernetes.io/gpu=true:NoSchedule" off for first two nodes just to accept pods.
harper (oncall): I'm creating the ASG now. Will post update when nodes join.
(5m pass)
harper (oncall): ASG created, instances launching. Waiting for kubelet join.
sanjeev: while that's happening, workaround to reduce user impact: enable fallback route in serving layer to route non-SLA customers to CPU pool. Running a patch to routing config.
kim (support): CS posting a status: "We are experiencing degraded GPU capacity in us-west-2 causing slower generations for some customers. Mitigation in progress." :hourglass_flowing_sand:
(7m pass)
leo: two nodes registered, but scheduler still shows pending pods due to GPU taint mismatch. I removed taint on one node (kubectl taint nodes <node> node.kubernetes.io/gpu:NoSchedule-). Pods are starting to schedule.
marta: good. But we should not leave taints off for long — that'd mix GPU workloads with other compute. We need proper node labels.
esteban (infra): Update: terraform mapping patch queued, but the IAM 403 still worries me. I tried to attach a tag via the autoscaling service role and got 403 unless I use a different role. There's likely a permission boundary added to the provisioner role. I'll escalate to security ownership.
harper (oncall): who can confirm the provisioner role's policies? Sanjeev?
sanjeev: I don't own IAM. Esteban, open an escalation with security, include logs. Meanwhile I'll keep routing fallback open.
esteban (infra): @security-team please triage: provisioner role attempting iam:AttachRolePolicy and iam:PassRole is failing in prod account. Logs attached: https://internal-log/redwood/iam/1719000000 (link).
(incident-bot): escalation created INC-171900 for IAM role failure and autoscaler impact. Pager on-call: sec-rotation.
kim (support): Customers DM'd: "what's ETA" — CS asking for tentative ETA. Harper, what's best guess?
harper (oncall): manual ASG recovered ~30% of required GPU capacity; routing fallback covers another 40% for non-critical customers. Full recovery depends on either terraform mapping patch or security fix for IAM. I'll estimate 1.5 hours conservative.
leo: I'm also seeing a flurry of node termination events on older nodegroups — preemptions? It could be ASG scale-in policy interfering. I'm going to increase min-size on the GPU ASG to avoid immediate scale-in.
sanjeev: good call. Also set autoscaler to ignore taints for new nodes temporarily and bump priority class for training workloads that are latency sensitive.
marta: after stabilization we need postmortem: timeline, root cause (twofold: bad launch template mapping + IAM policy drift), and action items: 1) add CI check to block terraform mapping drift, 2) restrict IAM changes without infra-owner approval, 3) autoscaler retry/backoff improvements and clearer error surfaced to ops console.
esteban (infra): security responded: they're rolling back the policy that introduced permission boundary for the provisioner. This should allow IAM attaches. I'll coordinate terraform apply once rollback completes.
(30m pass)
harper (oncall): security rollback confirmed; subsequent autoscaler attempts succeeded in creating nodegroup using lt v4. New nodes joined the cluster. Queue is down from 12k to 1.2k. API error rates dropping.
kim (support): CS updated status: mitigated, partial recovery, follow-up postmortem to come. Customers acknowledged.
leo: I'll keep the manual ASG up for 2 hours as buffer and then decommission.
sanjeev: closing mitigation actions: routing fallback disabled for eligible customers, min-size restored to normal, taints re-enabled on nodes.
marta: formal postmortem owner assigned: harper. Please include remediation and timeline.
harper (oncall): acknowledged. Creating postmortem doc now and will include incident_id INC-171900, timeline, and action items.
incident-bot: Incident INC-171900 updated: status=resolved->stabilized, severity=high, owners=[harper, esteban, marta], nextsteps=postmortem
(60m pass)
harper (oncall): final update: cluster stable, queue back to baseline. Closing thread but keeping ASG up until 17:00 PDT. Thanks all for quick triage. :trophy:
